column2: §RWarhammer:§! Venturers Lead in Person
Lead
A player in the Venturers may lead an expedition in person (Lead an Expedition, rank 2): better odds and greater rewards, and a real chance of dying in the jungle.
Sponsor Only
A player in the Venturers may only sponsor expeditions and send a captain. The AI may still lead in person.
Sponsor an Expedition

Put up gold, a ship and a captain from your court for a venture across the Great Ocean. More than half of all expeditions are never heard from again. The rest make their backers famous, and some make them rich.
Lead an Expedition
Sail with the venture yourself. The odds and the rewards both rise, and so does the chance that you never come home.
Hire Native Guides
Hire Skink trackers, castaways or the half-mad survivors of older ventures to lead your next expedition past the worst of the jungle.
Chart a Coast
Send one ship to map an unknown shore. Good charts make every later expedition safer, and the merchant houses pay well for copies.
You have no expedition out and have sent none in the last five years
You plan an expedition: pick a destination and a stake. A captain from your court will lead it.
You plan an expedition and lead it yourself. You will be away for most of a year.
Your next expedition has §Gbetter odds§!.
You have not sent a charting ship in the last five years
A ship sails to chart a far coast. It comes back in five to nine months, or not at all.
§RThe deadliest destination, and the richest.§! The Slann remember those who rob them.
More ships, more powder: §Gbetter odds§!, and twice the reward if it comes home.
A whole fleet: §Gmuch better odds§!, and the greatest reward if it comes home.
The expedition's odds §Gimprove§!.
The expedition's odds §Rworsen§!.
A deed of exploration, remembered by the Venturers.
A good harbour for a colony is marked on your charts.
§RThe Slann will remember this.§!
The fever passes, and the odds hold.
The guns hold, and the camp eats well for a week.
The line breaks, and half the camp goes under the feet.
The crew goes back to work, richer and no happier.
The riders are beaten off the beach.
The riders cut the landing party to pieces.
Half the time the floes open on a hidden bay.
Half the time the ice takes a ship.
A long, cold, expensive winter, but everyone lives.
Half the time the map is true.
Half the time it leads into a swamp.
For ten years your expeditions have §Gbetter odds§!.
Venture Sent
This Venturer has sent or led an expedition in the last five years.
On Expedition
This ruler is away across the sea with an expedition, and the realm drifts without them.
Guides Hired
Guides wait in port for this Venturer's next expedition.
Fresh Charts
This Venturer holds new charts of the far coasts. Their expeditions sail with better odds.
Charting Ship Sent
This Venturer has sent a charting ship in the last five years.
Treaty with a Temple-City
Like Marco Colombo at Tlax, this Venturer has made a treaty with a temple-city of the Slann. Its priests trade gold for steel, and its skinks guide the Venturer's people.
Famed Explorer
This Venturer led an expedition into the unknown and came home. Every tavern on the coast knows the tale.
The Green in the Blood
This Venturer came out of the jungle alone. The fever comes back every rainy season, and so do the dreams.
Jungle Idol
A squat golden idol with jade eyes, taken from a shrine deep in the green. It is worth a fortune. Its owners do not sleep well.
Navigator's Compass
A brass compass and a rutter of the far coasts, filled in by a navigator who sailed past the edge of every chart and came back.
Where Away?

The maps on your table end where the paint of the sea-serpents begins. Beyond them lie the jungles of Lustria and their temple-cities of gold, the green coasts of the Southlands and the black shores of Naggaroth.\n\nShips are waiting at [Root.GetVentureQuay], and [Root.GetVenturePatrons] want to know where you will send them.

The maps on your table end where the paint of the sea-serpents begins. Every Venturer worth the name has wondered what is beyond them, and you mean to find out for yourself.\n\nShips are waiting at [Root.GetVentureQuay]. [Root.GetVenturePatrons] think you mad to go in person. They may be right.
The coast of Lustria
A temple-city of the Slann
The Southlands
The cold coasts of Naggaroth
Not this year

Ships, powder, salt pork, beads for trading and gold for bribes. Every captain who ever came back from the far coasts says the same thing: whatever you take, take more.\n\nThe stake is lost if the venture is.
A modest purse
A proper fleet
Everything it takes
Think again

The green sickness came with the rains. Men sweat and rave through the night and are cold by morning, and your [Root.GetVentureCrew] whisper that the jungle itself is killing them.\n\nThere is bark in the chest that the physicians swear by, if you will pay what it is worth here.

A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName], months old and stained with sweat:\n\n'The green sickness came with the rains. We bury three a day. I can buy bark from the last ship in the bay at robbers' prices, or press on and pray. Tell me which.'
Press on
Pay for the physick

The ground shook before you heard them: a herd of Stegadons coming through the trees like a landslide, crushing everything in their path. Your [Root.GetVentureCrew] look to you. There may be time to form a line with the guns.

A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName]:\n\n'Beasts the size of houses came through the camp at dawn. We lost the stores and eleven men. They are coming back to the river every night to drink. I could hold a line with the guns, or we could move into the trees.'
Hold the line
Scatter into the trees
You wake to find the boats under guard and half the crew armed. Their spokesman is polite. They have had enough of fevers and lizards, and they want the ships and the way home.

A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName], in a shaking hand:\n\n'The crew has taken the boats. They want to go home. I can hang the ringleaders if I have the men for it, or promise them double pay out of your purse. Tell me quickly.'
Hang the ringleaders
Promise double pay
Talk them round

In a clearing no one has walked through for a thousand years stands a shrine of green stone, and on it is more gold than you have ever seen in one place. The guides will not go near it. Your [Root.GetVentureCrew] cannot look at anything else.

A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName]:\n\n'We have found a shrine plated in gold, older than anything at home. The guides say it belongs to the old gods of this land and that they will not stay if we touch it. The men say otherwise. Your orders?'
Strip the gold
Leave an offering and go quietly

Small blue-scaled creatures have watched the expedition from the trees for days. This morning they came out, with fruit, feathers and gold dust, and questions in a clicking tongue. They seem to know the way through the swamps.
Tribesmen of the Southlands came to the edge of the camp at dusk with water, dried meat and ivory to trade. They know the wells and the paths, and they want steel.
Trade steel for guidance
Drive them off
Dark riders on black horses have shadowed the landing party along the shingle for two days. Druchii. They are waiting for you to make a mistake.
A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName]:\n\n'Dark elf riders follow us along the shore. They take a man every night. I can fight them on the beach, or hide in the fog and lose a week.'
Fight them on the beach
Hide in the fog
The pack ice has closed behind the ships, and the rigging is white with frost. The old charts promise a hidden bay to the north, past the floes. They also promise a lot of things that are not there.

A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName]:\n\n'We are iced in. I can push north for the bay the old charts promise, or winter in a fjord, which will cost you dear in stores. The men are cold and afraid.'
Push north through the floes
Winter in a fjord

A man came out of the trees in rags, missing three fingers and most of his wits. He says he was with an older venture and buried its gold before the rest died. He has a map scratched on hide, and he will sell it to you for a passage home.

A letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName]:\n\n'A survivor of an older venture found us, mad as a hatter, with a map to treasure he swears he buried. It might be true. It might lead us into a swamp. Your call.'
Follow the map
Burn it

The green closed over the expedition one valley at a time. The fever took the strong, the swamps took the careless, and something in the night took the rest.\n\nNo one at [Root.GetVentureQuay] will ever learn what happened to you.

The ships were due home months ago. Then the season ended, and the next one. At [Root.GetVentureQuay] they have stopped watching for sails.\n\nThe venture is lost with all hands, and [venture_captain.GetBestName] with it. Your stake is gone.
The jungle keeps what it takes
The sea keeps its secrets

The venture is lost. But months after the last ship was given up, you walked out of the trees onto a trading post on the coast, alone, burned and thin as a rake, and talking to people who were not there.\n\nYou do not speak of what happened to the others. You do not sleep well either.
Home, at last

One ship of the fleet came home, with a third of the crew and you among them. There is enough in the hold to pay back half the stake, and enough stories to keep you in drinks for the rest of your life.
One ship of the fleet came home to [Root.GetVentureQuay], with a third of the crew and [venture_captain.GetBestName] among them. There is enough in the hold to pay back half your stake.
Better than nothing

The venture is home from Lustria: gold dust, jade, feathers, caged beasts nobody can name, and charts of a bay that would make a fine colony.\n\n[Root.GetVenturePatrons] are drinking your health. Your stake comes back twice over.

The venture is home from the Southlands: spices, ivory, ebony and gold, and charts of a sheltered harbour that would make a fine colony.\n\n[Root.GetVenturePatrons] are drinking your health. Your stake comes back twice over.

The venture is home from the cold coasts of Naggaroth: furs, amber, the treasures of a drowned Asur colony and charts of a bay no Druchii watches.\n\n[Root.GetVenturePatrons] are drinking your health. Your stake comes back twice over.
A venture well made

The fleet came home to [Root.GetVentureQuay] so low in the water that the harbour master thought they were sinking. Gold, jade, the plumes of birds no one at home has seen, and charts of a coast that could hold a kingdom.\n\nYour stake comes back four times over, and your name is on every tongue.

The fleet came home to [Root.GetVentureQuay] so low in the water that the harbour master thought they were sinking. Spices, ivory, gold and gems from the ruins of the old kingdoms, and charts of a coast that could hold a kingdom.\n\nYour stake comes back four times over, and your name is on every tongue.

The fleet came home to [Root.GetVentureQuay] heavy with furs, amber and Asur silver from a sunken colony, and charts of the whole cold coast, Druchii watchtowers and all.\n\nYour stake comes back four times over, and your name is on every tongue.
Fortune favours the bold

The jungle opened on a city of stepped pyramids plated in gold, so bright in the sun it hurt to look at. Saurus warriors stand on every stair. Somewhere at the top, the old ones who rule this land are watching.\n\nYou could take it. The gold would make you and [Root.GetVenturePatrons] rich beyond reckoning, and the Slann would never forget it. Or you could do as Marco Colombo did at Tlax: walk up the stairs with gifts, and talk.
Plunder the temple
Parley, as Colombo did

The charting ship is home at [Root.GetVentureQuay] with a chest of new charts: soundings, reefs, rivers, watering places and the bays where the Druchii do not watch. Every merchant house on the coast wants copies.
Keep them for our own ventures
Sell copies
The charting ship never came back. Perhaps a storm, perhaps a reef, perhaps a Black Ark or something worse. The sea does not say.
Another name for the harbour wall
the Hochmarkt quays of Marienburg
the harbour of Nordland
the docks of Luccini
the harbour of Magritta
the quays of Brionne
the harbour of Copher
the white quays of Cothique
the sea-gate of Barak Varr
the harbour of Haichai
the hidden harbour of the Norden
your own harbour
the merchant houses of the Directorate
the counting-houses and the Second Fleet
the merchant princes
the crown and the Church of Myrmidia
the dukes of the coast
the merchant princes of the souks
the Sea Wardens' houses
the clan guilds
the great trading houses
the jarls who remember Losteriksson
your backers

sailors and Nordland marines
mercenaries

sailors

Colonial Charter for [Title.GetBaseName]
$ORDER$$FIRST_ADJ$ Colonial Charter War for $OTHER_TITLE$
New Colony
This colony was founded less than ten years ago. The palisade is still green wood, the fields are half cleared, and the jungle wants it back.
Settlers from Home
Families from the old country have come to farm and build here, and the colony grows.

[venture_colony_title.GetName] is ours by charter and by the sword. The flag of [Root.GetPrimaryTitle.GetName] flies over a palisade of green wood, and [Root.GetVenturePatrons] want to know who will rule it.\n\n[venture_governor.GetBestName] has offered to stay and govern it in your name.
I will hold it myself
[venture_governor.GetFirstName] shall govern it

Ships from [Root.GetVentureQuay] have come to [venture_colony_site.GetName] crowded with families: farmers, smiths, priests and debtors, all of them wanting land in the new colony. Their passage is not paid.
Pay their passage
Let the colony grow on its own
Farmsteads
Cleared fields, fenced pens and granaries. In the jungle nothing lasts that is not fed, and every other work of the colony needs the food these bring in.
Fortifications
A palisade of hardwood, then earthworks, then stone: ditches, gun platforms and a gate that holds against Saurus and savages alike.
Colony Port
Wharves, a careening beach, warehouses and a customs house. Ships from home put in here, and the colony grows rich on what passes through.
Colony Monument
A statue of the founder, a shrine to the gods of home or a column carved with the names of the dead: something to tell the colony and the jungle who rules here now.
Colony Venue
A tavern, a fighting pit, a playhouse or a gambling den. Colonists far from home need somewhere to spend what they earn, and the colony takes its share.
Colony Capitol

A governor's palace, a council hall and a treasury. Only a colony with an established reputation (a Port, a Monument and a Venue) can raise a Capitol, and with it the colony becomes a city of its own.

The colony's §RPort is lost§! and must be built again.

The ground under [venture_colony_site.GetName] heaved for a night and a day. Walls cracked, the church bell rang on its own and the river changed its course. The natives say the Old Ones are turning in their sleep.\n\nThe colony can be rebuilt at once, if you pay for it.
Rebuild at once
Live in the ruins a while
A herd of Stegadons came out of the trees at dawn and went through the fields of [venture_colony_site.GetName] like a landslide. They are still grazing on what is left of the crops.
Hunt the herd
Build stockades and count the losses
The wet season got into the granaries of [venture_colony_site.GetName]. Half the grain is black with mould and the rest stinks. Ships in the harbour will sell food, at a price.
Buy food from the ships
Ration what is left
A brotherhood of deserters and dockside thugs has taken over the harbour of [venture_colony_site.GetName]. Every cargo pays them a toll, and now they want one from you.
Pay them
Crush them

The sea drew back from the beach of [venture_colony_site.GetName], further than anyone had ever seen it go, and then it came back as a wall of water. The quays are gone, and the ships in the harbour with them.
Rebuild the quays
Let the port go
Snakes in the beds, lizards in the pens and insects the size of a man's fist in the stores. The jungle has come into [venture_colony_site.GetName] through every crack.
Burn them out
Live with it

The Monument of [venture_colony_site.GetName] was found this morning smeared with paint and the glyphs of the old gods of this land. The colonists want blood. The priests want it washed clean before anyone sees.
Burn the nearest native village
Restore it quietly
The fever came to [venture_colony_site.GetName] with the flood season. The graveyard grows by a row a week.
Send for physicians from home
Close the gates and wait
Pamphlets in the taverns, whispers in the church, a mob at the governor's gate: someone is stirring the colonists of [venture_colony_site.GetName] against you, and they are paying well to do it.
Pay off the ringleaders
Hang them
Ships with no colours sit off the harbour mouth of [venture_colony_site.GetName] and take every ship that comes or goes. Their captain sends a note: for a fair price, they will go elsewhere.
Pay them to leave
Wait them out

Twelve men walked out of the jungle into [venture_colony_site.GetName] yesterday, the survivors of an expedition everyone gave up for lost three years ago. They are ragged and half mad, and their packs are full of gold. They pay their passage home and then some.
Welcome back
The founding day of [venture_colony_site.GetName] turned into a week of feasting, fighting and drinking in the colony's Venue. Nobody remembers the end of it, and everybody loves their lord for it.
Long live the colony
Natives have come out of the jungle to the gates of [venture_colony_site.GetName] with feathers, gold dust, fruit and medicines to trade. They want steel, cloth and salt.
Open the market to them
Drive them off
Colonists digging a new well in [venture_colony_site.GetName] struck an old chest full of coin: the hoard of some earlier venture that never came home.
Finders keepers
Rain at the right time and sun at the right time, no fever, no beasts and no raiders. In [venture_colony_site.GetName] they will talk about this year for a generation.
The gods smile on us
[Root.Location.GetAdjective] Temple Host
The Old Ones let the matter rest.
§RThe Slann will answer.§!
§RThe darts find their mark.§!
A dart grazes you.
The skinks are caught and killed.
Razed by the Old Ones
A temple host of the Slann burned this colony to the ground. The survivors are rebuilding among the ashes.
Defied the Slann
This Venturer's colony broke a Saurus host sent by the Old Ones themselves. No one on the coast has forgotten it.
The Omens

A comet hangs over the sea for a week. Every night you dream of something vast and still, behind your eyes, watching you without blinking. This morning there was a small jade tablet on your pillow, carved with glyphs no one at court can read.\n\nThe guides from Lustria know what it means, and they will not stay in the house. The Old Ones remember what you took from them.
Send gold to the temples in atonement
Give back what was taken
Let the toads do their worst

They came out of the jungle at dawn without a sound: rank on rank of Saurus warriors, Stegadons bellowing behind them and skinks in the trees. At their head walks an Oldblood scarred by a thousand years of war.\n\nThe Slann have answered. They have come for [venture_colony_site.GetName].
Man the walls!

Your taster died at supper, a tiny dart in his neck. Last night a guard was found in the garden, blue and swollen. The servants say they have seen small, bright-scaled shapes in the gardens at night, moving in silence.\n\nThe Slann have answered, and they have come for you.
Double the guard, whatever it costs
Let them come

[venture_colony_site.GetName] is gone. The Saurus burned the fields, pulled down the walls and the Capitol, smashed the Monument and drowned the Port. The survivors crawled back to the ruins when the host withdrew into the jungle as silently as it came.\n\nThe Old Ones have made their point.
We will rebuild

The temple host broke on the walls of [venture_colony_site.GetName]. For three days the Saurus came on without fear and without a sound, and for three days the guns cut them down. On the fourth morning they were gone, and the jungle was quiet.\n\nEvery port on the coast is singing about it. The Old Ones have nothing more to say to you.
Let them try again
Reputation Chosen
This Venturer chose a reputation in the last ten years.
You have not chosen a reputation in the last ten years
Choose a Reputation
Decide what the ports of the world say about you: a Conqueror, a Merchant Prince, a Scholar or a Saviour.
You choose what the ports of the world say about you.
Reputation: Conqueror
Every port on the coast knows this Venturer as a conqueror who takes new lands with the sword.
Reputation: Merchant Prince
Every port on the coast knows this Venturer as a merchant prince whose ships come home low in the water.
Reputation: Scholar
Every port on the coast knows this Venturer as a scholar who maps the unknown and brings home its secrets.
Reputation: Saviour
Every port on the coast knows this Venturer as a saviour who brings castaways and lost colonists home.
The Great Voyage

One last venture past the edge of every chart: west past Lustria to the end of the world, east round the Southlands to Ind and Cathay, or north through the ice. Few come back. Those who do are remembered forever, and their blood with them.
You plan the Great Voyage. It will take about two years.
You have at least six deeds of exploration
Some route of the Great Voyage has not yet been sailed
On the Great Voyage
This ruler is past the edge of every chart on the Great Voyage, and the realm has not heard from them in months.
Half the time it works.
Half the time it costs ships and men.
The Great Voyage turns for home. It will come back, but without its glory.
The Line of the Far Shore
The Line of the Far Shore descends from a Venturer who sailed west past Lustria, past the Sea of Dreams, to the edge of the world, and came home to tell of it.
The Line of the Sea Road
The Line of the Sea Road descends from a Venturer who sailed round the last cape of the Southlands to the courts of Ind and Cathay, and opened the sea road east.
The Line of the Northern Passage
The Line of the Northern Passage descends from a Venturer who found Losteriksson's dream, the passage through the ice past Naggaroth, and lived.
The Great Voyage

Every Venturer has looked at the edge of the charts and wondered. You have done more than wonder: you have been to the jungles, the temple-cities and the ice, and you have come back.\n\nThere is one voyage left that no one has made and lived. [Root.GetVenturePatrons] have put up the gold. Which way?
West, past Lustria, to the edge of the world
East, round the Southlands, to Ind and Cathay
North, through the ice, past Naggaroth
The fleet is fitting out at [Root.GetVentureQuay]: the best ships, the best [Root.GetVentureCrew] and two years of stores. Who will command it?
I will
Send the best captain we have

Past the last isles of Lustria the wind died. For weeks the fleet has drifted on a sea of weed, so thick a man could walk on it, under a sun that never seems to move. The water is going green in the casks. The sailors call it the Sea of Dreams, and some of them have started to talk in their sleep.

The last cape of the Southlands is all storms. Twice the fleet has tried to round it and twice the wind has thrown it back. The pilots say there is a way close in to the rocks. The pilots are also very drunk.
The ice has closed behind the fleet. Ahead there is open water, perhaps, past a wall of floes that groan and crack all night. Behind there is a long, cold winter in a fjord.
Push through
The slow way, whatever it costs

An island rose out of the sea at dawn, black and silent, and on it pyramids of a black stone older than any Slann temple. There is no one here. There has been no one here for a very long time. There is gold.

The fleet has reached a harbour no Old World chart has ever shown, and the king of the land, a prince of Ind who has never heard of the Empire, has sent a barge of gold and elephants to bring you to his court.

Under the ice of a dead bay lie the halls of the drowned: a Norse settlement older than Skeggi, or an Asur colony of Lothlakh lost when the sea took the coast. Its treasures are still there, under the ice and the dead.
Parley and trade
Take what is there
Read its secrets
Two years from home and the crew have had enough. They have seen too much, and buried too many. Tonight they came to your cabin, all of them, and asked you to turn for home.

The last letter from [venture_captain.GetBestName] came on a ship that turned back:\n\n'The men are at the end of their rope. If you have orders, send them now. In a month it will not matter what either of us wants.'
Hold them by force
Talk them round
Turn for home
The Voyage Comes Home

Two years after it sailed, the fleet came into [Root.GetVentureQuay] with half its ships and all its glory. In the holds: gold from the black pyramids, charts of the edge of the world, and a story that will be told as long as men go to sea.\n\nYour name is now one of the great names, and your children will carry it after you.

Two years after it sailed, the fleet came into [Root.GetVentureQuay] with silk, spices, jade, an elephant and a letter from a king of Ind. The sea road east is open, and it is yours.\n\nYour name is now one of the great names, and your children will carry it after you.

Two years after it sailed, the fleet came into [Root.GetVentureQuay] out of the north with furs, amber, the treasures of the drowned and a chart of the passage through the ice that Losteriksson dreamed of.\n\nYour name is now one of the great names, and your children will carry it after you.
Remember me
Lost Past the Edge

The Great Voyage never came home. Some say the fleet sailed off the edge of the world. Some say you found a land so rich that no one wanted to come back. At [Root.GetVentureQuay] they still look west when the sun goes down.

The Great Voyage never came home, and [venture_captain.GetBestName] with it. Your fortune went with them. At [Root.GetVentureQuay] the sailors say the sea at the edge of the world keeps what it takes.
The sea keeps its secrets

A single ship came into [Root.GetVentureQuay] with a handful of men, burned black by the sun or white with frostbite, talking of things past the edge of the charts that no one believes. The Great Voyage is over. It did not reach the end, but it went further than anyone before it.
Further than anyone
At every port where the Venturers drink, they talk about you. What do they say?
That I take new lands with the sword
That my ships come home low in the water
That I map the unknown and bring home its secrets
That I bring the lost ones home
